input.statement: Ferret's top-level `exclude` key accepts either a bare glob string or a full rule object ({pattern, scope: global|repository|session, reason?, effectiveFrom?}); patterns are matched with picomatch ({dot:true}) against repository-relative paths normalized to POSIX separators by `normalizePath`, and `effectiveExclusions(config)` = DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS (.git, node_modules, .venv, __pycache__, dist, build, coverage, .next, target, vendor) first, then the user's — exclusion is one-way and additive, so no scope can un-exclude.

Exclusion matching has an anchoring asymmetry decided by one regex in `matcherFor` (src/config/exclusions.ts): a pattern free of the metacharacters `*?[]{}!` is expanded into four alternatives — `p`, `p/**`, `**/p`, `**/p/**` — so a bare directory name means "that directory anywhere, and everything under it", while a pattern containing any metacharacter is passed to picomatch verbatim and is therefore anchored at the repository root (`docs/**/*.pdf` matches `docs/2024/report.pdf` but not `src/docs/2024/report.pdf`, and `benchmark/**` does not match `benchmark` itself). picomatch compiles each pattern to `^(?:…)$` and OR-matches an array, which is what makes the verbatim form root-anchored.

A trailing slash on an exclusion pattern is stripped before matching (`withoutTrailingSlash`, added in 0a66a88), so `secrets/` now means exactly what `secrets` means; before that fix it expanded to `secrets/`, `secrets//**`, `**/secrets/`, `**/secrets//**` and silently matched no path while still being reported as configured. A trailing slash is also stripped from a glob (`docs/**/` behaves as `docs/**`), and stripping happens before the metacharacter test, so `secrets/` still takes the four-way bare-name expansion.

As of 2026-09-07 an `exclude` rule is enforced on the read path, not at acquisition: `withholds`/`visibleEntities` in src/retrieval/access.ts call `evaluateExclusion` per row on any entity carrying a `path` attribute and return WithholdReason.EXCLUSION, and `walkForRepositories` (src/git/discovery.ts:194) skips excluded directories while searching for repositories — but nothing filters file contents on the way into the store, so excluded files are read from disk and their text retained. EPIC-135 measured this on the dogfood store (27 file entities, 1,463,485 bytes of excluded content) and is PROPOSED/deferred by owner decision, not implemented; `exclude` is distinct from `authorization.scope.exclude`, and since 6e26e97 a context pack reports an exclusion as `exclusion-rule` rather than as a permission denial.

An exclusion pattern beginning with `!` is refused at schema validation (`notNegated`, both the string shorthand and the rule object) because picomatch reads a leading `!` as negation and wraps the compiled regex as `(?:^(?!^(?:…)$).*$)` — `!keep` used to exclude every path except `keep`, silently turning the additive exclusion list into an allow-list. A `!` in any other position is an ordinary filename character, though it does count as a metacharacter for the expansion test and so suppresses the bare-name expansion.

input.conclusion: `exclude` is a top-level array of either a bare glob string or a full rule object ({pattern, scope, reason?, effectiveFrom?}), merged after Ferret's ten built-in defaults and matched with picomatch ({dot:true}) against POSIX-normalized repository-relative paths. Matching is asymmetric: a pattern with none of `*?[]{}!` is expanded to `p`, `p/**`, `**/p`, `**/p/**` (a bare directory name means that directory anywhere plus everything under it), while any pattern containing a metacharacter goes to picomatch verbatim and is therefore root-anchored — so `benchmark/**` misses `benchmark` itself and `docs/**/*.pdf` misses `src/docs/x.pdf`. A trailing slash is stripped before that test (fixed in 0a66a88; it previously produced `secrets//**` and matched nothing while still reporting as configured), and a leading `!` is now refused at schema validation. Enforcement today is on the read path (`withholds`/`visibleEntities` in src/retrieval/access.ts) plus the repository-discovery walk — not at acquisition: EPIC-135 documents that excluded file content is still read and stored, and it is PROPOSED/deferred, not implemented. I recorded five durable statements in Ferret covering the schema, the anchoring asymmetry, the trailing-slash rule, the negation refusal, and the read-versus-ingestion enforcement point.

`effectiveExclusions(config)` = `mergeExclusions(DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS, config.exclude)` (src/config/schema.ts:180); defaults are .git, node_modules, .venv, __pycache__, dist, build, coverage, .next, target, vendor, and come first so a user rule cannot displace them. Exclusion is one-way and additive across scopes.

`matcherFor` (src/config/exclusions.ts:114-120): `/[*?[\]{}!]/.test(pattern)` decides between `[pattern]` verbatim and the four-way expansion `[pattern, pattern/**, **/pattern, **/pattern/**]`. So a bare directory name matches at any depth; a metacharacter-bearing pattern is used as written.

Added in 0a66a88, whose message records that `secrets/` previously expanded to `secrets/`, `secrets//**`, `**/secrets/`, `**/secrets//**` and matched no path at all while still reporting as configured.

tests/unit/config-layers.test.ts:243-261 asserts both behaviours directly: `node_modules` excludes `node_modules`, `node_modules/pkg/index.js` and `src/node_modules/x.js` but not `src/index.js`; `node_modules/` behaves identically; `docs/**/` excludes `docs/2024/x.pdf`.

A leading `!` is refused by `notNegated` on both the shorthand and the rule form (src/config/exclusions.ts:49-58, 83-87), added in 0a66a88 because picomatch's negation wraps the regex as `(?:^(?!…).*$)` — `!keep` excluded everything except `keep`. `state.negated = true` at node_modules/picomatch/lib/parse.js:470. Test at tests/unit/config-layers.test.ts:263-273.

Read-path enforcement: `withholds` calls `evaluateExclusion` on any entity with a non-empty `path` attribute and returns `WithholdReason.EXCLUSION` (src/retrieval/access.ts:246-256); `visibleEntities` filters per row in the core because glob matching is not SQL (src/retrieval/access.ts:300-316). `effectiveFrom` is honoured via `options.at`, so a past question gets the past policy (src/config/exclusions.ts:159).

Discovery-path enforcement: `walkForRepositories` skips an excluded child with `SkipReason.EXCLUDED` (src/git/discovery.ts:194-197), fed by `effectiveExclusions(context.config)` plus caller rules (src/git/provider.ts:191, 252). This governs the directory walk that finds repositories.

No ingestion-path enforcement: `exclude` in src/indexing/indexer.ts refers to commit reachability tips, not paths. EPIC-135 §2 measured on the dogfood store on 2026-09-07 that excluded paths yielded 27 `file` entities, 43 `file_version` entities and 1,463,485 bytes of retained content, while every read surface correctly returned nothing.

EPIC-135 — Exclusion Enforcement at Ingestion is **PROPOSED**, P0, explicitly not implemented and deferred by owner decision on 2026-09-07 (docs/EPICs/EPIC-135-...md header and §16; docs/EPICs/README.md:217). So the read-path-only behaviour is what is true today.

answer.conclusion: Yes, as the repository stands. `matcherFor` strips trailing slashes before expanding a metacharacter-free pattern, so `secrets/` compiles to `secrets`, `secrets/**`, `**/secrets` and `**/secrets/**` — the directory and everything beneath it. This was a live defect until commit 0a66a88 (HEAD~1), where `secrets/` expanded to `secrets//**` and was accepted while matching nothing, so an answer resting on that older behaviour is superseded. Two caveats: the rule also catches any directory named `secrets` at any depth, and retrieval-time withholding keys on an entity's `path` attribute, so already-indexed evidence carrying no path is not filtered by it — an exclusion governs indexing and retrieval, never deletion.

`secrets/` contains no character matched by the metacharacter test /[*?[\]{}!]/, so once the slash is stripped it takes the four-form directory expansion rather than being used verbatim.

The trailing-slash handling was added by commit 0a66a88 (PR #227), whose message reads 'an exclusion written `secrets/` excluded nothing' and 'the failure mode was silence: the rule was accepted and reported as configured while excluding nothing'; 0a66a88 is HEAD~1 and src/config/exclusions.ts is clean in the working tree, so the fix is the current state.
